subject.title: Feishu announce delivery never succeeds for isolated cron jobs; fallbackUsed inconsistently rescues output

question: Should maintainers require a redacted live current-main Feishu isolated-cron reproduction before a fix PR, or is the current source and run-history evidence enough to start implementation?
rationale: The report is credible and high-impact, but source inspection shows several plausible failing layers and no integrated Feishu cron proof, so automation cannot safely choose the fix boundary alone.

options.title: Require live Feishu proof first
options.body: Ask for or run a redacted current-main Feishu isolated-cron proof that captures target resolution, outbound adapter invocation, delivery result, and `fallbackUsed` state before implementation.

options.title: Start a source-only investigation
options.body: Let a maintainer or repair worker instrument the cron and Feishu delivery path from source and add mocked adapter coverage before attempting live proof.

options.title: Fold into broader cron delivery semantics
options.body: Treat this as part of the existing cron execution/delivery-status cluster only if maintainers decide the primary Feishu failure is not distinct.

recommendation.title: Require live Feishu proof first
recommendation.body: Ask for or run a redacted current-main Feishu isolated-cron proof that captures target resolution, outbound adapter invocation, delivery result, and `fallbackUsed` state before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent combined Feishu and delivery-dispatch history for deciding the proof boundary.
